title: 86―EIGHTY-SIX
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: The Republic of San Magnolia claims to fight the Empire's Legion drones in a 'war without casualties', but its 'unmanned' drones are piloted by the Eighty-Six, young people of a marginalized group branded subhuman and confined outside the walls (Yen Press blurb; ANN). Shin is a skilled, grieving pilot and Lena a Republic officer who does not accept the official story (ANN). Manga adaptation of the light novel, discontinued after 3 volumes because of the artist's health (AniList, MU).
life_message: Every life counts; a society that hides the dead behind propaganda must be faced with their humanity.

content.note: Squads of mechs destroyed and pilots killed (ANN); War, Tragedy tags; art not gruesome (ANN).
Constant battle losses and dystopian setting (ANN; AniList Dystopian, Tragedy).
AniList Nudity at low rank (20); MU Romantic Subplot; ANN notes no fan service.
Dehumanizing slurs used by officials, framed critically (ANN).
Part of a light-novel and anime franchise.

dominant: Anti-dehumanization war drama; critique of state propaganda

frames.aligns: Dignity of every person against the Republic's 'subhuman' branding.
frames.concerns: War deaths of youths shown often.

frames.aligns: Mourning the forgotten dead; repentance of a complicit nation.
Truth-telling against a magistrate's unjust lie.
Authority that abuses its people is exposed.
Social holiness: the marginalized Eighty-Six seen as neighbors.
Respect for the dignity of every human being.
Exposes the lie of a 'war without casualties'.
Justice and mercy for the oppressed.

frames.concerns: Adharma of a cruel state shown at length.

frames.aligns: Compassion for those treated as disposable.
Systemic dehumanization exposed; not glorifying war (ANN).
Courage, sacrifice and loyalty of Shin's squad.
Seeing each person as truly human.
Defending the oppressed; equality of all.
Echoes of persecution and pikuach nefesh.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Human worth is inherent; the Republic denies it to the Eighty-Six (blurb, ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Military discipline valued, unjust state order critiqued.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Squad bonds; Lena extends loyalty beyond her own group (ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Caste-like exclusion is the evil shown (blurb).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Pilots live in survival mode on the front (ANN).

folkways.japan: Uses a European-styled setting; the pilots' stoic endurance and squad loyalty echo Japanese war-story conventions.

delivery.evidence: ANN: contrast between officers' callousness and the 86's humanity is 'effective'; neither reviewer calls it preachy.

personified.ideology: The Eighty-Six are subhuman and expendable
Conscience that refuses the official lie

delivery.note: The discriminatory view is shown as self-deception contradicted by evidence; reviewers did not call it a strawman.

winners_losers: The Eighty-Six receive the story's sympathy; the Republic's propaganda is the loser, though the manga ends early.
to_verify: Manga discontinued at 3 volumes; covers only the start of the novel story.
ANN review is of manga volume 1 only.
